Potentate

POH-ten-tayt · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Potentate is a ruler or monarch who holds great power, especially an absolute one.

The ambassador was granted a private audience with the potentate, who ruled the desert kingdom without any parliament to check his decisions.

Worked Example

Old travel journals describe European explorers being received by local potentates whose word was law across vast territories.

A potentate isn't just any ruler -- the word usually implies sweeping, largely unchecked power over a territory.

monarch

monarch: a sovereign ruler such as a king or queen

Antonyms

subject: a person ruled by a monarch or state, without power of their own

commoner

commoner: an ordinary person without noble rank

How Strong Is It? — ruler → potentate → tyrant

ruler vs. potentate

ruler vs. potentate: Ruler is a broad, neutral word for anyone in charge, whether a monarch, a mayor, or an elected president.

tyrant vs. potentate

tyrant vs. potentate: A tyrant goes further still, using absolute power cruelly and unjustly.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — potent-

root — potent-: powerful, able (Latin potens, potentis, 'powerful')

suffix — -ate

suffix — -ate: one who holds or performs a role (Latin -atus)

Put it together

Put it together: Potentate comes from Latin potens ('powerful') + -ate ('one who holds a role') -- literally 'one who holds power,' a ruler whose authority is total.

Use the root in a new word: potent

Use the root in a new word: potent: A potent remedy is an extremely powerful one -- potent shares potentate's same Latin root for 'powerful.'

Root Check

Word Choice

Potentate almost always describes an absolute ruler -- someone whose power isn't limited by a constitution, parliament, or voters. (This unit's puissant, by contrast, describes power or might itself, not the person who holds it.)
